title: The Cipher of Saint Alder's
premise: When a drowned man washes up at Saint Alder's coastal abbey wearing Sable Fairweather's own missing clothes, the insurance claim she's been quietly investigating becomes a murder case with her name stitched into it. The only witness, a recluse named Marlow Quill, supposedly died years ago—yet his cipher-encrypted letters keep arriving, each one naming a beneficiary of the abbey's vast inheritance trust. As Sable deciphers the trail, she realizes the 'dead' witness faked his death to expose how the abbey's trustees have been bleeding the estate dry, and that someone is killing to keep the ledger buried. The tide finally gives up what it took—a locked strongbox—forcing Sable to choose between protecting the friend who once shielded her and publishing a truth that will ruin them both.
about_author: Beatrix Joubert is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck insurance claims along the northern coast. She writes in a lighthouse-keeper's cottage and claims her best plot twists arrive on foggy mornings.

chapters.title: The Clothes on a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Sable Fairweather, POV. Called to Saint Alder's abbey to assess a flood-damaged insurance claim, Sable identifies the drowned stranger's clothing as items stolen from her own rented cottage. The horror of seeing herself on a corpse establishes her stake. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Reviewing the abbey's claim file, she notices years of quietly inflated losses—paper thefts hiding something larger. The abbey's bursar, Father Ambrose, deflects with practiced charm. Emotional beat: the investigator's thrill curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Man Who Is Officially Dead
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. A ciphered letter arrives, unsigned, referencing details only the original claim's witness—Marlow Quill, dead seven years—could know. Sable digs into Quill's death record and finds the tide listed as cause. Emotional beat: fascination overtaking fear.

chapters.title: Trustees of Saint Alder's
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. She interviews the three living trustees: Ambrose, shipping heiress Odile Vane, and the ailing matriarch Cecily Alder. Each describes Quill differently—as saint, fraudster, and stranger. Emotional beat: the sense that everyone is rehearsed.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Constable Idris Peale, POV. The police constable, half in love with Sable's stubbornness, shares the coroner's omissions: the drowned man's lungs held no seawater. He warns her off. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, tenderness under friction.

chapters.title: Cipher and Key
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Her photographic memory unlocks the cipher's pattern—it mirrors the abbey's stained-glass saints. The decoded fragment names Odile Vane and a sum: forty thousand pounds. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the realization the letters are a countdown.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Closet
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Someone ransacks her cottage—not for valuables but for the second set of clothes she'd bought. She realizes the killer needed a body dressed as her. Emotional beat: violation; invisibility was her armor, now stripped.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Odile Vane, drunk on brandy, admits the trust has been 'borrowed against' for years but swears she never touched the principal. She hints Quill discovered it and that Ambrose 'handled' him. Emotional beat: pity for a complicit woman.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Idris, POV. Idris traces Quill's last known days: a row with Ambrose, a boat hired at dawn, never returned. He finds the boat's registration filed under Sable's own cottage address. Emotional beat: doubt creeping toward the woman he trusts.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The cottage's former caretaker is found hanged, staged as suicide, holding a page of the cipher. Sable recognizes the staging—her own handwriting forged in the note. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Cecily Alder's Memory
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Dying Cecily Alder, lucid for one hour, recalls that Quill was her illegitimate son—and the trust's true heir. She gives Sable a key on a ribbon. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound, not gift.

chapters.title: The Key and the Cellar
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The key opens a bricked cellar alcove: Quill's hidden ledger proving the trustees' embezzlement, plus letters showing he faked his death to investigate from the shadows. The final page is torn out. Emotional beat: the truth almost whole, agonizingly short.

chapters.title: Ambrose Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Confronted, Ambrose doesn't deny it—he offers Sable a partnership, revealing he knows about her own falsified claim years ago, the secret that made her 'invisible.' Emotional beat: temptation and shame entwined; loyalty versus truth begins its war.

chapters.title: What Sable Buried
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Flashback chapter: the old claim Sable once misfiled to protect a friend from ruin, the origin of her pact with silence. Ambrose has held this over her all along. Emotional beat: the cost of her own compromised loyalty laid bare.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Kept the Secret
chapters.summary: Idris, POV. Idris discovers the 'friend' Sable protected is the missing torn page's author—Quill's old ally, now the abbey's groundskeeper, Tom Wicker. Wicker confesses Quill is alive, hiding in the sea caves. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Caves at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Sable finds Quill alive in the caves, half-mad, guarded by Wicker. He explains the drowned man was a hired impostor Ambrose killed and dressed in Sable's clothes to frame her and stop the investigation. Emotional beat: the witness everyone swore was dead, breathing.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns Against Them
chapters.summary: Sable and Quill, alternating POV. Ambrose's men seal the cave mouth as the tide rises. Quill, weakened, gives Sable the torn ledger page—naming the final beneficiary: Cecily Alder herself, the trust's silent architect. Emotional beat: desperation, then a devastating reframe of the villain.

chapters.title: The Matriarch's Design
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Escaping through the old smugglers' channel, Sable deciphers the full truth: Cecily built the trust to disinherit the corrupt trustees, and Quill's exposure would have destroyed her too. The dying woman's key was a test. Emotional beat: grief for a puppeteer she pitied.

chapters.title: Saint Alder's on Fire
chapters.summary: Idris, POV. Ambrose, exposed by Wicker's confession, burns the archive to destroy the ledger's duplicates and corners Sable in the burning scriptorium. Idris arrives; Ambrose falls through the collapsing floor into the flooded crypt. Emotional beat: climax—truth literally fought for in flame and water.

chapters.title: The Strongbox the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The receding tide uncovers the original strongbox Quill sank years ago—every document intact, the sea having kept the better archive. Sable holds the power to bury or publish everything, including her own old sin. Emotional beat: stillness after violence; judgment at hand.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Sable testifies, publishing the trust's truth and confessing her own falsified claim, surrendering her investigator's license. Ambrose survives to stand trial; Cecily dies knowing her design outlived her. Emotional beat: the cost paid willingly—truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable and Quill, closing POV. Months later, Quill, restored as heir, offers Sable a position as the trust's honest auditor. Walking the tideline, she reflects that invisibility was never an option—only a delay. Emotional beat: quiet redemption; the tide, at last, at peace.
